Workshop: Biohybrid Robotics for Cardiac Surgery and Functional Cardiac Assistance

Intended audience: Researchers, clinicians, students, and industry professionals in cardiac surgery, robotics, biomedical engineering, medical devices, and translational medicine. No combined clinical and engineering background is required.

Organizer:

Jie Wu, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, China
Zeyang Xia, Professor, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China
Jizhang Yu, Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, China
Beijia Zhang, PhD Candidate, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, China

Speakers:

Jie Wu, Clinical Needs and Translation of Biohybrid Robotics in Cardiac Surgery
Beijia Zhang, Physiological Sensing and Adaptive Control for Cardiac Biohybrid Assistance
Zhenyu He, Patient-Specific Simulation and Digital Twins for Cardiac Biohybrid Robotics
Jie Shen, Design of Biohybrid Robotic Systems for Cardiac Surgery
Xiaolin Wang, Postdoctoral Researcher, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Evolution and Application Trends of Cardiac Devices: From Conventional to Soft Systems
Selected contributors, Emerging Research in Biohybrid Robotics for Cardiac Medicine

List of topics: Biohybrid and soft robotic systems for cardiac intervention and assistance; device evolution and applications; actuators, sensors, tissue interfaces, sensing and control; patient-specific modelling and digital twins; imaging, safety, validation, clinical integration, and translation.

Tutorial outline: The workshop will review clinical needs and the development of cardiac assistive devices, including the transition from conventional to soft systems. Talks will cover sensing and control, patient-specific modelling, and the design and integration of biohybrid robotic systems.
Selected abstracts and a panel discussion will address emerging concepts, prototypes, methods, and translational considerations. The workshop seeks to support interdisciplinary exchange and identify practical directions for safe and clinically relevant cardiac biohybrid robotics.
